intro.displayText: The Club Hub's server knows every club in the Grove, but the page is empty. Your mission: get the page to ask the server, and show the clubs!
intro.speechText: The Club Hub's server knows every club in the Grove, but the page is empty. Your mission is to get the page to ask the server, and show the clubs!

recap.displayText: Your page and your server are talking. Your new word is full-stack: building the page and the server behind it.
recap.speechText: Your page and your server are talking. Your new word is full stack, which means building the page and the server behind it.

intro.displayText: Almost every app is a frontend asking a backend for data, and handling whatever comes back. The Junior League's API is ready; its page isn't. You'll build the standings table, make the division filter fetch again, and show the API's error instead of crashing on it.
intro.speechText: Almost every app is a frontend asking a backend for data, and handling whatever comes back. The Junior League's A P I is ready, but its page isn't. You'll build the standings table, make the division filter fetch again, and show the A P I's error instead of crashing on it.

recap.displayText: Your frontend and your API are working together, and the page copes when the answer is no. The gotcha to remember: fetch only fails when there's no answer at all. A 400 still resolves, so always check response.ok before you use the data.
recap.speechText: Your frontend and your A P I are working together, and the page copes when the answer is no. The gotcha to remember is that fetch only fails when there's no answer at all. A four hundred still resolves, so always check response dot ok before you use the data.

intro.displayText: Kids in the Grove want to start their own clubs! Your mission: add a form that sends each new club to your server.
intro.speechText: Kids in the Grove want to start their own clubs! Your mission is to add a form that sends each new club to your server.

recap.displayText: Your page can show clubs and start new ones. Your new word is POST: a request that sends something new for the server to keep.
recap.speechText: Your page can show clubs and start new ones. Your new word is post, which is a request that sends something new for the server to keep.

intro.displayText: Accepting writes is where APIs get risky: the server has to decide what a client may change, and explain clearly when a request is wrong. The league's API can read results, but it can't record them yet. You'll add the endpoints, guard them with a DTO and validation, and watch your standings page pick up the changes.
intro.speechText: Accepting writes is where A P Is get risky, because the server has to decide what a client may change, and explain clearly when a request is wrong. The league's A P I can read results, but it can't record them yet. You'll add the endpoints, guard them with a D T O and validation, and watch your standings page pick up the changes.

recap.displayText: Your API records, finds and deletes results, and refuses bad input with messages a form can show. The gotcha to remember: never bind an entity straight from a request. Bind a DTO, so the client can't set the id or anything else it shouldn't.
